scope: the diagnostic agent harness re-authored onto the version-2 vocabulary, and the #1055 baseline fixture re-pin
invariants: The harness registers the production v2 catalogue under each entry's own name and nothing else but the two generic backstops; no retired v1 name or refusal code is reachable on any surface it exposes.

The adapter converts only transport shape: an entry's description, family, touch paths and typed input schema survive to the tool list, and changed | unchanged | refused map onto accepted-with-changes, accepted-no-op and refused without re-shaping the owner's affected-entity collections.
A valid request that changes nothing is an accepted no-op: no changes, no history entry, no timestamp, and the original record identity (catalogue rule 4).
Every refusal leaves the document, the history and the redo stack byte-identical, and the caller's request record is never mutated.

Tier 0 is the production route's own stack in the route's own order - structure, domain, dependencies, compiler eligibility - run against the same assets; the harness keeps no second opinion about what a valid Show is.
Inside a transaction tier 0 is deferred to commit; a refused commit leaves the transaction open for correction and commits nothing.

Identity is never minted on the command path: every v2 owner takes the identities its caller supplies. Identity domains that are owner-scoped in v2 (keyframes, Transition participants, Group holds, appearance keys) are declared owner-scoped, not record-wide.
Opening a v2 record validates and lists; it never rewrites the caller's record into a second shape.

The committed coverage report and generic-only snapshot reproduce exactly from the v2 schema and the registry's declared touch paths, and every structural-cascade declaration names a command that really declares that touch.
A v2 record round-trips whole through .pxlshow: the importer normalizes nothing away.
partitions: Tool surface: catalogue entry, generic backstop, session/ceremony tool, retired v1 name (absent).
Outcome: changed, unchanged (accepted no-op), refused at the command, refused by deferred tier 0 at commit, refused by the protocol schema before any owner runs.

Pattern reference: resolvable stock, unknown stock (hard error in every mode), resolvable personal through inline source, unresolvable personal existing before the edit (tolerated in editing-session mode), unresolvable personal newly introduced (refused).
Referent source: direct id, hovered, selected, at_ms, at_playhead, pattern name, ordinal within a Zone; resolutions unique, ambiguous, none.

Document fault at the session boundary: dangling Clip instanceId, missing Layer, missing Zone in the active Layout, malformed routing operator, duplicate Pattern instance, same-Layer overlap, unknown stock id.
Turn disposition: committed, asked, refused, incomplete, nothing-applied, commit-refused after the one repair opportunity.
Baseline fixture outcome: changed, refused for a same-Layer neighbour, .epe export error from an unresolvable Library namespace.
Installation contract shape: complete coverage, incomplete, overlapping, out-of-range, fractional endpoint, over-capacity pixel count, unknown physical Zone.
sequences: MCP (#1029): open_show -> create_layers -> create_clips -> remove_clips -> set_show_end exactly 30000 -> add_property_tracks -> commit -> outcome -> export and reopen (test/catalogueSurface.test.ts, test/grammarMcp.e2e.test.ts).

Deferred-validation repair: resize the first Clip -> create an exactly adjacent second Clip -> add a section-scoped view-brightness track on it -> insert a participant Crossfade between them (every owner accepts) -> commit refuses with the compiler's own section-scoped message -> remove_transition inside the still-open transaction -> commit succeeds as one history entry.
Unrepaired variant of the same sequence: the repair pass changes nothing, the turn ends commit-refused, no candidate is exported and the request record is unchanged.
Resolve-then-operate: set_editor_context -> resolve_reference (hovered) -> resize_clip by the returned id -> describe_show reports the new duration.

Stable resize retry: an ordinal-resolved resize binds exactly one Clip identity; a second mutation, a malformed call, a lifecycle call or an extra argument makes the turn ineligible; the retained binding re-executes on moved, reordered, renamed later state.

Baseline fixture run: every fixture converted to v2, exported as .pxlshow and .epe at a fixed stamp, one scripted bridge turn over real HTTP/NDJSON/MCP, exported again, hashes compared against the committed pin.
oracles: The reopened .pxlshow through parseShowFileBundle({ acceptV2: true }) and the reopened .epe through parseEpe, including its PXLBLZ show stamp - never a generator internal.
The MCP client's own tool list, input schemas and resource contents over a real client/server pair.
The exported session record after commit, and its equality with the pre-edit record after undo.
The session's history entries and their summaries, and the redo stack after a refusal.
The committed coverage artifact compared byte-for-byte with the generator's output.
The committed fixture evidence file, compared path by path against a fresh run.
The engine's own property evaluator at a named time, read back through evaluate_property_at.
The 47-record parity census report (npm run show:v2-parity), unchanged.
redEvidence: The slice began with 81 failing harness cases across 22 files at base 15ed7a50; every one was driven to green by re-authoring the case on a v2 fault or v2 argument shape, never by weakening an assertion. The inventory and its root-cause grouping are in the coordinator handoff for this issue.
grammarCoverage.test.ts failed at module load (SHOW_STRUCTURE_COMMANDS is not iterable) because it imported the v1 registry; re-authored on SHOW_COMMANDS_V2 and the v2 report.

showsMcpServer.e2e.test.ts asserted a 77-name v1 tool list; the observed 71-name v2 list was checked entry by entry against SHOW_COMMANDS_V2 before being recorded, and a separate case now asserts each retired v1 name is absent.

The re-authored authoringValidation suite was written case by case against the v1 suite it replaces; its header names, for every v1 case not carried over, either the test that already covers it or the retired premise that removes it.
faults: catalogue.ts: map the owner's `unchanged` outcome onto a refusal -> catalogueSurface.test.ts 'unchanged: an already-satisfied valid request is an accepted no-op' fails; restored.

evaluate.ts: drop the personal-Pattern remedy mapping -> showEvaluate.test.ts 'rejects user-library references with an explanatory error' and 'tolerates an unresolved user reference in editing-session mode' both fail; restored.

experiment/cases.ts: reintroduce the retired name move_clip in one corpus case -> showCommandsV2/nameMapReplay.test.ts 'leaves no retired version-1 name in the dictation corpus cases' fails; restored.

grammar/coverage.ts: add a structural-cascade declaration for a touch path insert_time does not declare -> grammarCoverage.test.ts 'keeps every structural cascade declaration anchored to a command that declares that touch' fails; restored.

grammar/session.ts: close the transaction when a commit is refused -> grammarMcp.e2e.test.ts 'drives a transaction round trip ... including a refused commit' fails. authoringValidation.test.ts did not catch it, so its invalid-final-candidate case was strengthened to assert the open transaction; the mutation then fails there too. Restored.
residualGaps: The version-2 admission path runs no Portable capability check. A portable-2d Show naming the 3D-only stock Pattern AuroraSphere validates, prepares and compiles, where v1 refused it with portable-compatibility. validatePortableShowCompatibility is reachable only from showPreviewArtifact.ts and showAuthoringValidation.ts, both v1-only. Pinned as current behaviour with a RESIDUAL comment in test/bridgeAuthoringValidation.test.ts; an engine-only port slice is dispatched separately and will flip that pin.

The version-2 admission path runs no Installation coverage check. Incomplete, overlapping, out-of-range, fractional and over-capacity physical pixel ranges all validate and stay authorable, where v1 diagnosed each. showPreparedStageV2.ts computes the coverage fact onto the prepared capture's presentation but nothing turns it into a refusal. Pinned as current behaviour with a RESIDUAL comment in test/authoringValidation.test.ts; reported to the epic, not repaired here, because making the harness stricter than the route would restore exactly the second opinion this rewrite removed.

The browser baseline (e2e/agent-baseline.auth.spec.ts) is not re-authored onto the v2 route in this slice. Its 2536 lines seed version-1 rows through POST /api/shows and read them back through version-1 helpers (mainPlacements, firstMain, watchShowWrites), so every sequence drives the v1 editor while the bridge it talks to is version-2 only. Diagnosis, the reproduction and a scoped plan are in docs/reference/agent-editing-baseline.md; the browser-sequence utterance catalogue in baseline/scripts.ts was trimmed to the entries this repository's offline suites actually run, rather than guessing at v2 argument shapes nothing exercises.

schemas/show-record-v2.provisional.schema.json still describes itself as experimental input not wired to production decoding, persistence, admission, compilation, import or export. It is now the structural validator behind production admission. Routed to the #1043 documentation sweep.

The harness no longer reports the v1 artifactBlocker advisory for an oversized target pixel count, because the v2 preparation owner has no such advisory and takes no caller-supplied target count; recorded in test/showEvaluate.test.ts.
Final authoritative committed-tip suites and the exact-range review are the coordinator's, not this worker's.
